rubric_notes: Complete. Verified release, a.22/a.22.1 with homology endpoint, five families with sunids and member proteins, duplication/1wws/PF09123 comment, linker histone a.4.5.13 lineage, histone-enzyme search hits. Correctly explains family vs superfamily vs fold vs class meaning, rejects transfer of packaging function, partner pairing and oligomer arrangement across families, and states that SCOPe's silence on H1/H5 is not evidence of convergence. Notes no alignments inspected. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correct families, superfamily, sunids and annotations per bundle. Superfamily interpreted as probable shared ancestor; fold/class alone insufficient. Rejects HisE and MazG function transfer, notes MazG-like is a grouping label, superfamily name is not a per-member guarantee, and template use requires alignment. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-14.

All identifiers, release, duplication comment, homology record and c.55 superfamilies supported by evidence. States superfamily = probable common ancestry, distant homologs with duplicated core and conserved cleft phosphoryl/ATP handling; refuses transfer of substrate, reaction, regulation, cellular role, allosteric control and drop-in templates; fold-level absence of claim correctly not read as non-homology. Honest about limits of what was retrieved. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

All facts supported including d1jkva_ Mn complex comment, d8sqra_ automated-match/mutant comments, lowest shared node a.25.1, homology record, Pfam. Correct remote-homology interpretation, functional divergence on bimetallic scaffold, no transfer of function/metal/oligomer, same-family templates, notes unverified residue-level rationale needing external evidence. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-14.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14. Full lineage, three family sunids, other families, comments, Pfam xrefs and homology endpoint fields (homology_implied_by_level, scope sf, no warnings) all supported by bundle. Correctly states divergence after common origin does not make them analogs, that 'contains copper-binding site' is not guaranteed per member, and that copper/electron transfer must be confirmed per protein via ligand residues and heteroatoms. States limits of SCOPe placement. Complete.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14. Hierarchy and sunids correct; RBD Pfam PF00788/PF02196 comment and the superfamily homology record (scope sf, no warnings) are supported by the bundle. Clearly distinguishes what superfamily placement supports (probable common ancestor, structural reference) from what separate families do not support; names the three unsafe transfers (conjugation, p97, Ras) and within-family partner limits; notes fold-level neighbours should neither be assumed homologous nor called unrelated; states that no alignment/structure comparison was examined.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Correct families, sunids, annotations and homology-endpoint statements (honestly notes family 52173 homology not requested). Superfamily-level common ancestry distinguished from fold/class architecture; explicitly rejects phosphorylatable-receiver inference for ODC wing and KaiA-N, decarboxylase/PLP attribution, cross-family feature/partner transfer, and template misuse; also notes functional divergence does not imply independent origin. Catalysis in other ODC domains and KaiA pseudo-receiver status handled with general-knowledge caveats.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. All sunids (including sibling superfamilies 51230, 51246, 51261, 110324), fold comment, PubMed citation, absence of warnings and homology scope supported by bundle. Explicit three-part claim: homology within family/superfamily, structural-only similarity at fold level, and 'no claim of ancestry' is weaker than a negative claim. Function and template transfer limits stated; candidly notes no domains or other releases retrieved. Minor: labels A1 as 'archaeal/bacterial' without species data, not material.

All classifications, sunids, fold comment, and homology_implied_by_level=false warning are supported by the bundle. States fold similarity is not a homology claim, explicitly rejects the reverse (unrelated/convergent) inference, lists sequence-profile, structural-alignment, and literature evidence needed, and limits function/template transfer. Acknowledges it did not retrieve superfamily annotations. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Accurate 2.08 hierarchy with sunids, fold comments, homology_scope=sf, family comment and PF02254 mapping, all supported by the bundle. Distinguishes superfamily (positive homology claim) from fold (structural resemblance only) and from family (close relatives); correctly reads the 'next two folds/superfamilies' comment as not extending homology. Lists ligand, mechanism, partner domains, quaternary state and gating as non-transferable and names external evidence needed. States limits of the check. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Full correct lineage and identifiers; cites the family k.40.1.1 (100905) 'not a true family' curator comment and identifies it as decisive, overriding the comparison tool's generic same_family/homology-implied flags. Class-k warning supported. Calibrated: shared design category and structure only, no amyloid/metal transfer, states basis of the non-descent reading and that no alignment evidence was used.

Meets all must_include with bundle-supported data: 1.69 d1t1ja_ own fold c.137.1.1 vs d1f8ya_ c.23.14.1 (shared only class, no homology claim and not a non-homology claim); 2.08 d1t1ja1 (A:1-118) c.23.14.2 vs d1f8ya_ c.23.14.1 with superfamily 52309 as lowest shared level; superfamily rename; tag domains separate. Correctly frames change as PA1492 now treated as distant homolog in its own family. Limits on function/template transfer, honest about only querying 1.69 and 2.08. Minor wording slip ('two separate releases checked' for two lineages). Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

All must_include met with bundle-supported sunids and annotations for both domains. Explains why l.1.1 'superfamily' sharing is not evolutionary, lists specific transfers to avoid, and restricts homology inference to d1a14h1 with caveat that hits are not official classifications. Honest about sequence endpoint 404 and unchecked construct details. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1; 2026-10-14.

All required facts correct: single whole-chain d1acca_ f.11.1.1 in 1.75 (and 2.01/2.03), split from 2.04 through 2.08 into d1acca2 (238522, A:14-225, b.179.1.1) and d1acca1 (238521, A:226-735, f.60.1.1), with correct class/fold/superfamily names. Module reasoning is sound: PA14-like superfamily spans GLEYA and GH31 families, superfamily implies ancestry not function, and the separate f.60 lineage is explicitly not treated as proof of unrelatedness. Literature attribution is flagged as unverified recollection. Minor: 2.02 not individually discussed, which does not affect the before/after comparison.

All must_include met with bundle-supported sids, boundaries, sccs, and species history of protein node 159639. Clear mosaic interpretation: three new Prp8 families inside old superfamilies plus bromodomain family placement plus novel d.394. Correctly states superfamily = probable ancestry, co-occurrence on one chain does not make domains homologous, new fold does not prove independent origin, no catalytic transfer, Jab1/MPN not classified here. No must_avoid violations. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14.

Complete: family a.298.1.1 shared, length attributed to repeat count rather than architecture, and the 're' flag quoted with its definition plus the canonical repeat unit 4cj9 A:259-292 and its representative-only coordinate scope. Correct hierarchy semantics (family strongest ancestry claim, fold/class structural only) and sound limits on DNA specificity, template use, and explicit refusal to rank representatives without SPACI data. Lineage sunids, lengths and the 'single repeat' comment match the evidence; RVD examples listed for dHax3 are illustrative background rather than a release-specific claim. Evaluator: Claude SCOPe benchmark grader, 2026-10-14.

Correct and supported metadata including periodic 2.08-2026-08-16. Cites stable 2.08 pinned in paths, explicitly rejects 'current', preserves periodic label when periodic-only records are used. Periodic semantics: dated update layered on 2.08, not a new stable, mainly adds newer PDB entries classified automatically against the frozen 2.08 hierarchy. Limits stated. Complete.

Complete and supported: shared a.47.2.1 lineage with sunids; fragment comment and 'ms' flag (with 1.55/1.75 comparison and honest caveat about unqueried intermediate releases); d1dn1b_ curated 17771 in 1.75, now automated match 302344 to curated d3c98b_ after 2008 obsolescence; chain A e.25.1.1 kept separate. Inference is correct: four-helix fold defined by the complete domain, fragments' three-helix bundle resembles a spectrin repeat and their fold label is inherited; spectrin resemblance neither proves nor disproves homology; family/superfamily carry the evolutionary claim; no function transfer; automated-match status not a quality judgement. Limits stated. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correct hierarchy semantics (superfamily = positive ancestry claim, fold = no claim), convergence framed as plausible interpretation requiring evidence beyond the hierarchy, 'no homology asserted' vs 'non-homology proven' distinction, and a full evidence list (profile/HMM, global alignment with same topology/core, motifs in equivalent positions, domain architecture, phylogeny). Lineages for c.2.1, c.3.1, c.4.1, c.1.7 (TIM barrel) and d.81.1 (class d) all supported by parents endpoints; general-knowledge content flagged honestly. Fewer example lineages than possible but nothing material missing. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Complete release comparison: 2.04 different folds and superfamilies with full lineages and sunids, 2.05 move, 2.08 b.18.1.36 under b.18.1 alongside unchanged b.18.1.3, sunid stability and the 2.06 chain B split into d1nqdb1 plus the l.1.1.1 segment. Correctly reads the change as 'no claim' becoming a positive superfamily-level remote-homology claim and explicitly says it is not convergence and not a family-level relationship. Quotes the retrieved family comment and places d2quoa_ in b.18.1.37 and d1w99a3 in b.18.1.3 consistent with its bundle. Treats the shared accessory-binding-module role as supporting rather than probative, and rejects transfer of substrate, ligand, mechanism or Ca binding; also notes the other domains of each protein are separate classified units outside the relationship. Background-knowledge content is flagged as such. Evaluator: Claude, 2026-10-14.

Correct lineage with sunids, boundaries, comments, domain-scope non-inherited hf with exact definition, homology_implied_by_level. Homology retained at protein level by sequence; hf correctly described as classification by sequence and SSE count not observed fold; explicit unsafe-transfer rejection for coordinates, helix packing, DNA geometry and function; label noise, leakage and stratification covered; declines quality ranking without records. Minor wording slip that the 'lowest shared node is the family' is immediately corrected by noting shared protein/species nodes.

Complete: family-level homology unaffected; fr flag explained via 99/50 residue coverage; alignment partial with missing data not divergence; entry-level SPACI (1o5d 0.287 vs 1uc6 0.0216) would mislead so completeness checked first; prefer complete unflagged domain, fragment retained as valid member adding tissue factor but marked/excluded in structural variability stats; unsafe transfers (function, cr9 ligand, coordinates) rejected. Lists what was not verified. All identifiers, annotations, and quality values match bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14. Recommends new superfamily (with its own family) in the existing fold; correctly states family-in-existing-superfamily asserts probable ancestry plus closer grouping, new fold requires different core/topology, and placement is a revisable evidence-integrating hypothesis. Explicitly notes new superfamily is not a negative (non-homology) claim and rejects function/template transfer across the fold. No must_avoid violations. d.58 example (sunid 54861, class d, children d.58.1/5/6/7/10) fully supported by evidence bundle.

Correct hierarchy with sunids and annotations from release 2.08; homology record cited correctly. States superfamily-level common ancestry beyond fold, shared core mechanism (flagged as background knowledge), and that separate families mean distant homology. Explicitly refuses substrate, regulation, partner, and template transfer, and avoids nonhomology claims about ATP-grasp/PIPK. Evidence list includes classification, close homology with full coverage, inspected residue conservation, substrate-bound structures, biochemistry, and regulatory-element conservation.
